data.narrative:
OBSIDIA Semiconductor is a seed-stage company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The broader comp universe includes 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, with notable private companies including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Two standard valuation methods were assessed but deemed inapplicable. Peer-median analysis failed because the narrow seed-stage filter within Chips & Semiconductors yielded insufficient datapoints—only 0 same-stage peers, 1 adjacent-stage peer, and 0 similar-tier peers were identified, falling short of the 3-datapoint minimum threshold. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied because OBSIDIA's revenue is not on file, a typical constraint for private companies; the public semiconductor sector median P/S of 21.4x across the three public comps cannot be meaningfully applied without a revenue baseline.

The analysis reaches no triangulated valuation range at this stage. The core limitation is data scarcity: neither peer-derived multiples nor public-market anchoring are calculable with the available information. To progress, OBSIDIA would require either disclosed revenue figures (to enable public-comp application) or additional seed-stage private comparables within semiconductors. The frontier-tech nature of the sector and the crowded competitive landscape (8 other private peers identified) suggest valuation will be highly dependent on technology differentiation and investor conviction rather than precedent multiples.
